what_happened: Scene: layout 10, grey 4-slot (two-pair) toaster, bread in slot 3 (right pair, pair 1); the two lever handles are on the front face. Stage 0: from 114 to ~370 the open gripper rested on the toaster top above the bread (continuous toaster contact) without moving any lever. 370-392 the fingertips pushed down on the bread top. That pushed the bread and the pair-1 carriage down to 0.46 (bread -2.3 cm), well short of the 0.9 needed to switch on, and both sprang back by 480. 490-720 it tried to grasp the untoasted bread from above. The bread was centred between the open fingers at 608-688, with contacts at 490-516, 524-534, 569-597 and 694-709. The fingers closed at 630 (0.058), 678 (0.023) and 721 (0.001), each time without lifting the bread (lift 0-1 mm; the bread sat too low in the slot). Each push nudged the carriage to 0.11-0.13. After 728 the fingers stayed closed. 760-1240 the fist moved around the toaster front and top (toaster contact 1070-1226) without touching either lever handle. It then lifted away (1400) and hovered in front of the toaster until 2000. The lever was never pressed; the bread stayed in the toaster, untoasted.
causal_chain: rested on the toaster top 114-370 -> pushed the bread down (carriage 0.46, below the 0.9 switch-on) -> repeated attempts to grasp and pull out the untoasted bread (490-721, no lift) -> fingers closed for good at 728; never used the lever handle -> toaster never on, stage 0 failed
self_recovery: none effective: the only lever motion was a side-effect of pushing on the bread.
uncertain_about: Whether the 370-392 push on the bread was an intended 'press' (pressing the bread down instead of the lever) or the first grasp approach.
